title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics and parity + v1.101.1 version bump
author: Maya Patel
description: Summary: This PR standardizes the auth, retry, and streaming ergonomics across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs and bumps SDK package versions to v1.101.1. Motivation: Multiple downstream teams reported surface-area inconsistencies between SDKs (auth configuration shape, retry policy defaults, and streaming consumer ergonomics). These inconsistencies cause developer confusion and duplicate example code. The change consolidates behaviors and adds small adapter layers where language differences require it. Changes include: 1) Auth: unify credential priority order (env > config file > explicit param) and add a single 'Credentials' helper across SDKs. 2) Retries: introduce a common RetryPolicy concept (max_retries, backoff_strategy, jitter) and align default backoff values with platform SLOs. 3) Streaming: provide a higher-level streaming iterator/async iterator API in TypeScript and Python, and a channel-based consumer in Go; all three expose consistent event shapes (data, error, done). 4) Parity fixes: bring missing helpers from TypeScript into Python/Go (e.g., request_metadata(), token_source adapters). 5) Version bumps: package versions updated to v1.101.1 with updated changelogs. Migration notes: - Auth: existing calls continue to work but users that passed positional auth params should prefer the new Credentials helper for future-proofing. - Retries: default behavior tightened (fewer immediate retries); any consumers that relied on prior retry aggressiveness should pin previous versions or opt out by configuring RetryPolicy. - Streaming: minimal API adapter included to keep backwards compatibility for most use cases; advanced users should migrate to the new iterator/channel primitives for simpler error handling. Testing: added unit and integration tests across all SDKs and added e2e test fixtures that mimic long-lived streams and intermittent auth failures. Related: ENG-1890 (SDK parity), ENG-1921 (retry tuning), SUP-4421 (customer-reported inconsistency).
